speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in view of strong hiring demand for engineers and technology specialists alongside rising retrenchments among Professionals, Managers, Executives and Technicians (PMETs) reported in the annual job vacancies report, what are the key factors driving this mismatch in the labour market.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And whether the Ministry has any plans to improve our job matching and reskilling interventions, so that we can better align displaced PMETs with available roles in these new areas of engineering and technology?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And how does the Ministry then assess the effectiveness of such efforts to date, if they already exist?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: In fact, to better understand the hiring landscape today, the hiring demand for PMETs remains higher than the number of PMET retrenchments.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: And many of the in-demand PMET jobs are actually in finance and infocomm.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: And in these particular sectors, the PMET retrenchments remain low relative to entire workforce size, and there remain ample opportunities available.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: To that point, the Government will always continue to provide support for workers to upskill and reskill into these roles.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: So, I encourage them to take it up.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
text: Yes, my question simply means that whether the Ministry or WSG will consider developing or working with professional institutions for those particular professions or trade to develop programmes that are relevant directly to the industries, rather than looking at programmes that are developed by the universities or the other academic institutions?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Yes, I thank the Member for the question.
